moves.name: Height-map 3D
moves.summary: Read the 2D image as a height map and raise it into a lit terrain you can orbit.
moves.summary_ko: 화면 밝기를 하이트맵으로 써서 카메라로 돌려 볼 수 있는 3D 지형으로 만들어요.
moves.guide: Keep the existing 2D pass but render it into a square texture (createPingPong(512, 512, {depth: true})) instead of the screen: every ctx.resolution/u_resolution, viewport and bindFramebuffer(null) in that pass (including helpers) must use the texture's size and framebuffer; then rebind null + reset the viewport for the 3D draw. Draw ctx.utils.geometry.plane(2, 2, 255, 255) (XZ plane, normal +Y; at most 255 segments, since its indices are Uint16) and in the vertex shader displace y by luminance × u_height, sampling with textureLod(map, vec2(uv.x, 1.0 - uv.y), u_smooth) after gl.generateMipmap + LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR each frame, so Smooth is a cheap blur. If the scene has its own height field (a sim state or noise field), prefer it to luminance. Normals in the fragment shader from normalize(cross(dFdx(v_pos), dFdy(v_pos))) (flip to face +Y), one key light + soft ambient + a little specular, colored by the original texture. ctx.utils.createOrbitCamera (phi ≈ 0.95, distance ≈ 3, autoRotate ≈ 0.12), depth test on, clear color + depth. In portrait keep the horizontal view: vp = mat4.multiply(cam.getProjectionMatrix(a, a < 1 ? 2·atan(tan(fov/2)/a) : fov), cam.getViewMatrix()). Uniforms: Height, Smooth.

moves.name: Raymarched SDF
moves.summary: Rebuild the shapes as signed distance fields: soft shadows, ambient occlusion, infinite detail.
moves.summary_ko: 형태를 SDF로 다시 만들어 소프트 섀도와 AO가 있는 3D로 렌더링해요.
moves.guide: Translate the scene's main forms into a 3D SDF in a fullscreen fragment shader (paste ctx.utils.glsl.SDF_SHAPES and SDF_OPS: sdBox, sdSphere, opSmoothUnion(d1, d2, k)…; k must stay > 0, min ≈ 0.001, or it divides by zero). Pass the orbit camera's getEye()/getTarget() as uniforms and build the ray per pixel from forward/right/up and tan(fov/2); in portrait multiply that by 1/aspect so the subject stays in frame. Loop to a constant (e.g. 256) and break at u_steps; hit when d < 0.001·t; step d·0.9. For repeated forms (grids, cities) with varying sizes, clamp the distance to the cell wall (min(d, wallDist + 0.05)) or rays skip into neighbours. Normals by central differences, soft shadows (k ≈ 8, ~40 steps), 5-tap AO, fade to the background color with distance so step-starved far hits don't show. Carry the original palette, emissive details and motion (time, audio, controls) into the SDF and its shading so it still feels like the same piece. Expose Steps (int, ~150) and Blend (smooth-union radius).

moves.name: Point cloud
moves.summary: Turn the image or mesh into thousands of glowing points floating in space.
moves.summary_ko: 이미지나 메쉬를 수많은 점으로 바꿔 3D 공간에 띄워요.
moves.guide: Sample the source: for an image or video, one point per texel on a grid (e.g. 256×256) with z from luminance or a depth map; for a mesh, its vertices or random points on its triangles. Draw gl.POINTS with gl_VertexID from an empty VAO (bind one: gl.createVertexArray()), fetching color/position in the vertex shader (texture()/texelFetch on the live texture) so animated or video sources update for free; apply the same uv flip/crop the original pass used. Point size must be in world terms: gl_PointSize = max(1.0, u_size * u_resolution.y / 1000.0 * 10.0 / gl_Position.w) at orbit distance ~3 (the bare h/1000/w gives sub-pixel points). Round soft points: discard outside the circle, color × exp(-3r²) × ~0.6, additive blending (ONE, ONE) with depth test and depth write off, dark clear color. Orbit camera (autoRotate ≈ 0.15); in portrait widen the vertical fov (fov' = 2·atan(tan(fov/2)/aspect), via getProjectionMatrix × getViewMatrix) so the cloud stays in frame. Uniforms: Point size, Depth, Jitter (snoise drift from ctx.utils.glsl.SIMPLEX_3D).

moves.name: Depth parallax
moves.summary: Estimate depth with Depth Anything V2 and turn a still photo into a 3D parallax scene.
moves.summary_ko: Depth Anything V2로 사진의 깊이를 추정해 입체 패럴랙스로 만들어요.
moves.guide: Needs an image asset. recipe_search "depth" first; otherwise python_run Depth Anything V2 (catalog_get depth-anything-v2 for packages and weights license) on the image and write a 16-bit grayscale depth PNG to out/. In the scene, displace a dense plane (ctx.utils.geometry.plane with ~512 segments) by the depth texture, color it with the photo, and drive the camera with a small orbit (or mouse parallax) so the layers separate. Fill stretched edges by fading alpha where the depth gradient is steep. Save the depth step as a recipe. Tell the person the model downloads once and is slow without a GPU.

moves.name: Gaussian splatting
moves.summary: Render with 3D Gaussian splats: soft, photographic volumes from scans or from your own points.
moves.summary_ko: 스캔 데이터나 장면의 점을 3D 가우시안 스플랫으로 렌더링해요.
moves.guide: Use Spark (MIT, three.js-based): const THREE = await ctx.utils.import("https://esm.sh/three@0.186.0"); const { SplatMesh, SparkRenderer } = await ctx.utils.import("https://esm.sh/@sparkjsdev/spark@2.2.0?deps=three@0.186.0"). new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas: ctx.canvas, context: ctx.gl, antialias: false }), a THREE.Scene with new SparkRenderer({ renderer }) added, PerspectiveCamera following createOrbitCamera getEye()/getTarget(); renderer.setSize(w, h, false) on resize; renderer.resetState() before render. A capture (.ply, .splat, .spz, .ksplat, .sog): new SplatMesh({ url: ctx.assets[name] }). Else from the scene's points/vertices/texels: new SplatMesh({ maxSplats: n, constructSplats: (p) => p.pushSplat(center, scales, quaternion, opacity, color) }) (THREE.Vector3/Quaternion/Color), then await mesh.initialized. Scales are σ (drawn to ~2.8σ): keep them ≈0.15× point spacing (anisotropic along the surface), or it looks defocused. Colors are linear (color.setRGB(r, g, b, THREE.SRGBColorSpace)). To animate: mesh.packedSplats.setSplat(i, …) per frame, then packedSplats.needsUpdate = true; mesh.updateVersion(). In cleanup set ctx.gl.clientWaitSync = () => ctx.gl.ALREADY_SIGNALED before dispose(), else Spark's pending readback rejects ("Error: undefined") into the next run. Uniforms: Splat scale, Opacity. Keep under ~1M splats.

moves.name: Volumetric rendering
moves.summary: Treat the pattern as a density field and raymarch light through it: smoke, nebula, fog.
moves.summary_ko: 패턴을 밀도 볼륨으로 보고 레이마칭해 연기·성운·안개처럼 렌더링해요.
moves.guide: Define density(p) in a box from the scene's own content: extrude the 2D field through the thin axis with a falloff that grows with the value (a·exp(-y²/2s²), s ≈ 0.03–0.06 of the box; thicker smears into streaks), or keep a simulation in a 3D texture (gl.texImage3D, R16F, 64–128³) or a 2D atlas of slices. Copy R32F state into an R16F LINEAR texture each frame (R32F isn't filterable everywhere). Fullscreen pass: ray = invert(proj·view of createOrbitCamera) · vec4(ndc, 1, 1) from getEye(); slab-intersect the box; 64–128 steps from a per-pixel jitter (interleaved gradient noise + u_frame); Beer–Lambert: col += T·(lit + emissive)·(1 − exp(−σΔt)), T *= exp(−σΔt); 6–8 steps toward one light for self-shadowing; Henyey–Greenstein g ≈ 0.3; color from the original palette, emissive where it was bright; ACES; a near-black background added as bg·T. Drag now orbits, so move painting to a modifier key or drop it. For portrait, widen fovY so the box keeps its width. Uniforms: Density, Absorption, Thickness, Glow, Light direction (pad), Steps. Render at half resolution into a target and upscale if slow.

moves.name: PBR + IBL
moves.summary: Physically based materials lit by an environment: metal, glass-like coat, real reflections.
moves.summary_ko: 물리 기반 재질과 환경광(IBL)으로 금속·코팅·반사를 사실적으로 표현해요.
moves.guide: Shade with Cook–Torrance: GGX distribution, Smith-Schlick geometry, Schlick Fresnel with F0 = mix(0.04, albedo, metallic); energy-conserving diffuse. Keep the scene's own colors as albedo (Base color tints them). Environment: either a procedural studio evaluated by direction (a dark gradient with a warm lit floor below the horizon, otherwise metals go black underneath, plus 2–3 soft rectangular lights whose edges widen with roughness, divided by ~(1 + 3·roughness) so rough isn't brighter), or prefilter one in setup into a small cubemap mip chain by roughness. Specular IBL with the split-sum (analytic DFG fit, e.g. Karis), diffuse from the env at the normal with roughness 1, plus one key light matching the brightest softbox; clearcoat as a second Fresnel-weighted sharp env lookup. Remove the scene's own gamma, then ACES and 1/2.2. With three.js or Babylon, switch to MeshStandardMaterial / PBRMaterial and a PMREM-filtered environment instead. Uniforms: Base color, Metallic, Roughness, Clearcoat, Env intensity.

moves.name: Path tracing
moves.summary: Trace light bounces progressively for soft shadows, color bleeding and glossy reflections.
moves.summary_ko: 빛의 바운스를 누적해 소프트 섀도, 컬러 블리딩, 광택 반사를 만들어요.
moves.guide: Progressive accumulation in a ping-pong RGBA32F target (enable EXT_color_buffer_float). Each frame trace 1 sample per pixel (PCG hash seeded by pixel + frame, jittered sub-pixel), up to 4 bounces: Fresnel-weighted choice of a GGX glossy lobe or a cosine diffuse one, Russian roulette after bounce 2. Light it with one rectangular area light plus a dim sky, and sample the light directly at every diffuse hit (next-event estimation, shadow ray against the scene), counting light hit by bounces only after glossy ones. Without this a small light is pure noise. Clamp each sample (≈4) against fireflies. Mix into the accumulation with weight 1/(n+1); reset n when a key of eye, target, uniforms and size changes; while the scene animates use max(1/(n+1), 0.15). Intersect an SDF (turn generated meshes back into their source, e.g. a smooth-min of the balls) or analytic primitives; for big triangle meshes use three-mesh-bvh. Add a floor so shadows and color bleeding show. Don't reuse a scene uniform's name for shader arrays. Display: small bilateral blur (Denoise), exposure, ACES, gamma; ctx.publish the sample count. Uniforms: Bounces, Exposure, Denoise.

moves.name: Post-processing (bloom, DOF, grain)
moves.summary: Bloom, depth of field, film grain, vignette and tonemapping for a filmed look.
moves.summary_ko: 블룸, 피사계 심도, 필름 그레인, 비네팅, 톤매핑으로 영화 같은 질감을 더해요.
moves.guide: Enable EXT_color_buffer_float and render the existing scene into an HDR target (createPingPong(w, h, {internalFormat: RGBA16F, type: HALF_FLOAT, depth: true}), recreated on ctx.resized) instead of the screen. Remove the scene's own gamma, let highlights go above 1, and write distance to the eye in alpha (clear alpha to a large value) for depth of field. Bloom: soft threshold, 5–6 half-size levels down with a 13-tap filter, then tent-upsample back up with blendFunc(ONE, ONE). Depth of field in its own pass (circle of confusion from distance vs Focus, golden-angle spiral, ~48 taps, radius from the frame height). Then the composite reads the DOF result: chromatic aberration (sample r and b offset toward the edges; doing it on the un-blurred source leaves colored halos), + bloom, exposure, vignette, ACES, film grain (per-frame hash, midtone-weighted, ~0.04), sRGB. Keep each stage switchable and subtle by default. Uniforms: Bloom, Exposure, Focus, Aperture, Vignette, Aberration, Grain.

moves.name: Toon shading + outlines
moves.summary: Flat, stepped light with ink outlines, like an illustration or anime frame.
moves.summary_ko: 계단식 셰이딩과 잉크 아웃라인으로 일러스트·애니메이션 느낌을 내요.
moves.guide: Shade from smooth vertex normals: flat facets (dFdx normals) turn bands into sawteeth, so compute normals (manifold-3d calculateNormals(0, ~25°), or average per vertex) and keep creases sharp. Quantise diffuse into 2–4 bands with fwidth-wide smoothstep edges, add a rim light and a hard specular dot. In one multi-target pass (createPingPong(w, h, {count: 2, internalFormat: RGBA16F, type: HALF_FLOAT, depth: true}); clear each attachment with clearBufferfv) write the toon color (alpha = shadow amount) and normal + distance to the eye. Ink pass: Sobel on normals (creases) and on distance divided by the center distance (silhouettes, scale-free), offset px = width·min(w, h)/1000 so landscape and portrait lines match; empty pixels (distance 0) get the paper color. Optionally hatch the darker bands with screen-space diagonal lines in ink. Uniforms: Bands, Outline width, Ink color, Paper color, Hatching.

moves.name: Flow-field particles
moves.summary: Let thousands of particles stream along the image's own currents, leaving trails.
moves.summary_ko: 수많은 파티클이 화면의 흐름(그래디언트·컬 노이즈)을 따라 흐르며 궤적을 남겨요.
moves.guide: Render the scene into a source target (bind it where its last pass binds null). Particles: RGBA32F NEAREST ping-pong (256²/512²/1024²; needs EXT_color_buffer_float), xy uv, z age, w lifetime 2–6 s. One full-screen update pass: velocity from the scene's luminance gradient over a few pixels (h/250, so lines and grain don't dominate), rotated 90° (−g.y, g.x) to follow contours, scaled up (~×40; gradients are tiny) and normalised together with a little curl noise (finite differences of snoise, ctx.utils.glsl.SIMPLEX_3D) so flat areas still move; step = Speed × h/500 px × dt·60. Respawn at a hash position when out of frame or age > life. Draw gl.drawArrays(gl.POINTS, 0, n) with bindVertexArray(null), fetching texelFetch(pos, ivec2(gl_VertexID % side, gl_VertexID / side)); colour from the source at the particle, alpha ~0.35 faded over life, alpha-blended into an RGBA16F trail target first multiplied by (1 − Fade); point size max(1, h/720 × 1.5). Add a little of the scene under the trails to keep it readable. Uniforms: Count (select), Speed, Fade, Noise scale, Show scene.

moves.name: Feedback loop
moves.summary: Feed each frame back into the next, slightly zoomed and rotated: echoes and tunnels.
moves.summary_ko: 이전 프레임을 줌·회전해 다시 그려 잔상과 터널을 만들어요.
moves.guide: Render the scene into a target (bind it where its last pass binds null). Keep an RGBA16F ping-pong for the feedback (8-bit stalls at faint values instead of decaying). Each frame: prev = feedback sampled through a small inverse transform done in pixels around a centre (zoom ~1.01, rotate ~0.3°/frame; centre = pointer once it has moved, else the middle; black outside the frame), hue-rotated in YIQ, × Decay (~0.96). Combine by brightness, not by adding: k = smoothstep(−0.04, 0.04, lum(scene) − lum(prev)), out = mix(prev, scene, k); an opaque scene's background otherwise builds up to white. Write to the other buffer, swap, blit to the screen. Clear on ctx.resized and on a Clear button. Uniforms: Decay, Zoom, Twist, Hue drift, Clear (button).

moves.name: Reaction–diffusion
moves.summary: Grow living Turing patterns (spots, stripes, coral) seeded from the current image.
moves.summary_ko: 지금 화면을 씨앗으로 그레이-스콧 패턴(점·줄무늬·산호)을 키워요.
moves.guide: Gray–Scott on an RGBA16F ping-pong grid (512 on the long side, aspect from the first frame, kept on resize, cover-fit; clear to A=1, B=0). Render the scene into a target first (bind it where its last pass binds null). 8–16 iterations per frame (set the grid viewport inside the loop), 9-point Laplacian (0.2 edges, 0.05 corners, −1 centre), Da 1, Db 0.5. Scene mask m = smoothstep(0.08, 0.2, max over a few samples per cell of |scene − ground colour|): max, because a cell spans several pixels and lines are thin; difference from the ground, not brightness, so light grounds work and vignettes stay under the threshold. Seed on the first frame and on Reseed with B = 0.6 on a random ~40% of masked cells (a solid seed just fills flat), and each frame sprinkle B into rare masked cells so newly drawn parts catch. Regional params: K += 0.006·(1 − m), so patterns grow where the scene is and starve elsewhere. Display t = smoothstep(.1, .35, B) → mix(ground, palette(t) × shading from B's gradient, t), then the scene's strokes on top. Uniforms: Feed (0.0545), Kill (0.062), Speed (iterations), Show line, Reseed (button).

moves.name: Physics simulation
moves.summary: Give the shapes mass and let them fall, collide and pile up; drag them with the mouse.
moves.summary_ko: 형태에 질량을 줘 떨어지고 부딪히고 쌓이게 해요. 마우스로 집어 던질 수도 있어요.
moves.guide: 2D: matter-js; 3D: Rapier (catalog_get rapier / matter-js for the pinned import and the example that uses it). Build bodies from the scene's shapes (boxes/spheres/convex hulls approximating them), a floor and walls fitted to the current aspect (rebuild walls on ctx.resized), step with a fixed dt (1/60, max 3 substeps), and draw with the scene's existing rendering using the bodies' transforms. Mouse: pick and drag with a spring joint. Uniforms: Gravity, Bounce, Spawn (button).

moves.name: Pixel sorting
moves.summary: Sort runs of pixels by brightness along a direction: melting, streaked glitch art.
moves.summary_ko: 밝기 구간의 픽셀을 한 방향으로 정렬해 녹아내리는 글리치를 만들어요.
moves.guide: Render the scene into a target (bind it where the scene's last pass binds null). For any angle copy it into a rotated sort buffer sized |w·cos|+|h·sin| × |w·sin|+|h·cos| (RGBA8, NEAREST, alpha 0 outside the frame) so the sort always runs along x, and rotate back to show it. Each frame do N odd–even transposition passes in a ping-pong: pixel x pairs with x+1 when (x+parity) is even, else x−1, flipping parity every pass; swap when out of order by luminance and both are inside the interval mask (alpha 1, Low ≤ lum ≤ High), so edges stay intact. Use drawFullscreen for every pass (a bare drawArrays draws nothing: the quad VAO is unbound after each drawFullscreen) and set the viewport to the sort buffer inside the loop. It converges at N px per frame, which looks good animated; restart from the fresh frame every few seconds (ctx.time), on Reset and when the angle changes. Pick thresholds from the scene: on dark scenes Low ≈ 0.1 streaks the sky and keeps the lights, ≈ 0.03 melts everything. Uniforms: Threshold low/high, Direction (angle), Passes per frame (~24), Re-sort every (s), Reset (button).

moves.name: Datamosh
moves.summary: Smear the image along its own motion like a corrupted video codec: pixels melt and bloom.
moves.summary_ko: I-프레임 없이 모션 벡터만 남은 코덱처럼 화면을 움직임 방향으로 번지게 해요.
moves.guide: Live version: render the scene into a source ping-pong (write = this frame, read = last frame; swap after). Block size B = Block size × h/720 px. Motion: one fragment per block into an RGBA16F NEAREST target of ceil(w/B)×ceil(h/B); brute-force block match over integer pixel offsets (±6 steps of B/8 px, 4×4 luminance samples, SAD plus a small |d|² penalty so flat areas pick 0), storing d with cur(x) ≈ prev(x+d). Each frame write output = previous output sampled at x + d_block(x)·Mosh (texelFetch the vector at floor(px/B)), with R/B sampled at ±0.35·d for chroma slip ("P-frame without I-frame"). Put the true frame back in a block when hash(block, random seed) < Refresh·dt, and everywhere on the first frame, on resize and on Keyframe. Output is a canvas-sized RGBA8 ping-pong blitted to the screen. Steady motion (rotation, scrolling, drift) moshes best; static scenes just freeze. For a rendered video file instead, ffmpeg can drop I-frames from an AVI/MPEG-4 Part 2 encode (command_run, catalog_get ffmpeg). Uniforms: Mosh amount (~1.5), Block size (16), Refresh rate (~0.15/s), Keyframe (button).

moves.name: Dither & halftone
moves.summary: Print-like rendering: ordered dither, halftone dots or a 1-bit palette.
moves.summary_ko: Bayer·블루 노이즈 디더링이나 CMYK 하프톤으로 인쇄물 같은 질감을 내요.
moves.guide: Post-process: render the scene into a target (bind it where its last pass binds null), then one full-screen pass. Bayer/blue noise: pixelate to cells of max(1, round(h/300 × Pixel size)) px, sample the cell centre, go to linear (pow 2.2), add (threshold − 0.5)·~0.35, pick the nearest palette colour (luma-weighted distance), back to sRGB. Bayer 8×8 from bit interleaving. There is no blue-noise asset: generate a 64² rank texture in setup by void filling (repeatedly take the empty cell with the lowest toroidal Gaussian energy, σ≈1.9; ~100 ms), upload R32F NEAREST. Make the first palette the scene's own colours (its colour uniforms + line colour/white) so it stays recognisable; add ink-on-paper and a 4-green handheld. Halftone: CMYK dots on grids at 15°/75°/0°/45°, cell ≈ h/120, radius ∝ sqrt(coverage), 1 px smoothstep edge; multiply real ink colours (cyan .0,.63,.89; magenta .89,0,.52; yellow 1,.92,0) over paper and use light grey replacement (K = smoothstep(.35, 1, 1−max(rgb))): pure CMY primaries and K = 1−max look neon or muddy. Uniforms: Style (select: Bayer, Blue noise, Halftone), Pixel size, Palette (select).

moves.name: ASCII art
moves.summary: Rebuild the image from characters picked by brightness, terminal or newspaper style.
moves.summary_ko: 밝기에 맞는 글자로 화면을 다시 그려요.
moves.guide: Render the scene into a target (bind it where its last pass binds null). Glyph atlas in a 2D canvas: one row of square tiles, one per character of the ramp (" .:-=+*#%@", " ░▒▓█", " 01" or the person's text), white bold monospace at ~0.95 × tile on transparent, uploaded RGBA with UNPACK_FLIP_Y false (flip y inside the tile when sampling). Cell = round(min(w, h)/80 × Cell size) px, from the shorter side so portrait doesn't get 40 huge columns; rebuild the atlas whenever cell size or charset changes (covers ctx.resized). Post pass: average 4×4 samples per cell, map luminance with a gain and a soft gamma (pow ~0.75), since dark scenes otherwise become all spaces and dots; glyph = floor(l × count); multiply the glyph alpha by the cell colour (colour mode: colour / max channel × l; mono: one phosphor colour). Uniforms: Cell size, Charset (select), Color mode (toggle mono/color), Brightness.

moves.name: Audio reactive
moves.summary: Make it listen: bass, mids and treble drive motion, color and scale live.
moves.summary_ko: 마이크 소리의 베이스·미드·트레블이 움직임과 색, 크기를 바꿔요.
moves.guide: Add "microphone" to inputs (or play an audio asset with ctx.utils.audio.play). Map ctx.audio.bass to scale/impulse, mid to motion speed, treble to sparkle/detail and level to brightness; smooth with an attack/release follower (fast up, slow down) so it pulses instead of flickering. For spectrum-driven visuals use ctx.utils.audioTexture(). Uniforms: Sensitivity, Smoothing, and which band drives what if useful.

moves.name: Beat sync (librosa)
moves.summary: Analyse a song with librosa (beats, downbeats, sections) and cut the visuals on the beat.
moves.summary_ko: librosa로 곡의 비트·다운비트·구간을 분석해 박자에 맞춰 화면을 바꿔요.
moves.guide: Needs an audio asset (ask for one if there is none). recipe_search "beat" first; otherwise python_run librosa (catalog_get librosa) to write out/beats.json: tempo, beat times, downbeats (every 4th, phase from onset strength), onset envelope (~50 fps) and section boundaries (librosa.segment.agglomerative on chroma/MFCC). In the scene, play the song with ctx.utils.audio.play(name, { output: true }) (or add a timeline of the song's duration so offline renders stay in sync), and drive events from the beat list using ctx.time: a decaying pulse after each beat, bigger changes on downbeats, a palette or form switch per section. Publish the current beat/section. Save the analysis as a recipe.

moves.name: Stem-reactive (Demucs)
moves.summary: Split the song into drums, bass, vocals and other with Demucs; each stem drives its own layer.
moves.summary_ko: Demucs로 드럼·베이스·보컬을 분리해 악기마다 다른 레이어를 움직여요.
moves.guide: Needs an audio asset. python_run Demucs (catalog_get demucs; htdemucs, slow on CPU) to split it, then librosa per stem to write out/stems.json with an RMS envelope per stem at ~60 fps plus drum onsets. In the scene play the original mix and read each stem's envelope at ctx.time: e.g. drums → impacts/shape, bass → scale/camera push, vocals → color/glow, other → texture. Use a timeline of the song's duration so offline export lines up. Save it as a recipe so the next song is one call.

moves.name: Music video
moves.summary: Give it a song: beats, sections and stems become a timed, cut-to-the-beat video you can export.
moves.summary_ko: 곡의 비트·구간·스템 분석으로 박자에 맞춰 편집된 영상을 만들어 내보내요.
moves.guide: Needs an audio asset. Run the beat-sync analysis (and stems if the person wants instrument-level motion). Build a timeline scene with duration = song length: one look per section (reuse the current scene as one of them and vary palette, camera and form for the others), hard cuts or fast transitions on downbeats at section boundaries, continuous reaction to the envelopes inside sections, keyframes for the big moments so the person can retime them. Then offer to record it offline (viewport_record, mp4, 1080×1920 for reels or 1920×1080) with the song as the soundtrack.

moves.name: Hand tracking
moves.summary: Track hands with the webcam (MediaPipe) and let fingers push, pinch and paint the scene.
moves.summary_ko: 웹캠으로 손을 추적해 손가락으로 밀고, 집고, 그리게 해요.
moves.guide: Use MediaPipe HandLandmarker as described in the ctx reference (inputs: ["camera"]). Map index-finger tips to forces or brushes, pinch distance (thumb–index) to a grab/size control, and hand openness to intensity. Show the camera faintly (mirrored) or not at all. Smooth landmark positions over a few frames. Fall back to the mouse when no hand is visible so the scene still works.

moves.name: MIDI mapping
moves.summary: Wire knobs and pads to the controls so it can be played live on stage.
moves.summary_ko: 노브와 패드를 컨트롤에 매핑해 무대에서 연주할 수 있게 해요.
moves.guide: Add "midi" to inputs. Map the scene's main uniforms to CC 1–8 (first eight knobs), pads/notes 36–51 to triggers (bursts, palette switches, cuts), pitch bend to a sweep; blend the MIDI value with the on-screen control (use the control until that CC first moves). Tell the person the mapping in the reply and publish the last CC/note.

moves.name: Pen-plotter SVG
moves.summary: Turn the piece into clean vector strokes and an optimised SVG ready for an AxiDraw.
moves.summary_ko: 라인으로 바꾸고 vpype로 최적화해 AxiDraw로 바로 그릴 수 있는 SVG를 만들어요.
moves.guide: Generate line work from the scene (contours/hatching of its luminance, flow-field streamlines, or the existing lines), render it as lines so the person sees the plot, and export the polylines (asset or python_run). Then vpype (catalog_get vpype) to merge, simplify, sort and fit to A4/A3 with margins: write out/plot.svg. Keep stroke count reasonable (< 20k segments). Uniforms: Line density, Pen width (preview).

moves.name: Seamless loop
moves.summary: Make the motion loop seamlessly over N seconds, ready for a GIF, reel or LED wall.
moves.summary_ko: 움직임이 N초마다 이음새 없이 반복되게 해서 GIF·릴스·LED 월에 바로 써요.
moves.guide: Add a timeline with loop: true and duration T (default 6 s). Replace free-running time with phase = ctx.time / T and drive every motion with periodic functions of phase: angles 2π·phase, noise sampled on a circle (noise(cos 2πφ·r, sin 2πφ·r, z)), or crossfade the last 15% into the start. Simulations: keep preserveStateOnLoop false and seed deterministically. Offer to record one loop (viewport_record).

moves.name: SSAO
moves.summary: Screen-space ambient occlusion: soft contact shadows in creases and corners.
moves.summary_ko: 틈과 모서리에 부드러운 접촉 그림자를 넣는 스크린 스페이스 앰비언트 오클루전이에요.
moves.guide: Raster scenes: render normals (view space) and linear view depth into an RGBA16F target in the same pass as color (createPingPong(w, h, {count: 2, internalFormat: RGBA16F, type: HALF_FLOAT, depth: true}); clearBufferfv per attachment). SSAO pass at half resolution: reconstruct view position from depth and the inverse projection (cam.getProjectionMatrix(aspect)), 16–32 hemisphere kernel samples scaled toward the center, oriented by the normal with a per-pixel random rotation (4×4 hash), project each, compare depths with bias ≈ 0.02·radius and a range check smoothstep(0, 1, radius / |Δz|). Blur 4×4 depth-aware, then multiply only the ambient/indirect term in the composite (not direct light), and keep it subtle. Radius in world units relative to the subject's size. Raymarched SDFs: skip the buffers and use 5 samples along the normal (ao += (h − map(p + n·h))·w). Uniforms: AO radius, Intensity, Samples. Don't name the kernel array like a scene uniform.

moves.name: Perspective warp / corner pin
moves.summary: Warp the whole picture onto any four corners: projection mapping onto a wall, a box or a screen at an angle.
moves.summary_ko: 화면 전체를 네 모서리에 맞춰 원근 변형해요. 벽·박스·기울어진 스크린에 프로젝션 매핑할 때 써요.
moves.guide: Render the scene into a canvas-sized target (bind it where its last pass binds null). Final pass: a perspective-correct homography, not two affine triangles (those kink along the diagonal). Compute the 3×3 matrix mapping the unit square to the four corner points (square-to-quad: dx1 = x1−x2, … standard Heckbert formula) in JS each frame, invert it, and in a fullscreen fragment shader map each output pixel p (0..1, y up) through H⁻¹ (homogeneous divide) to the source uv; black outside [0,1]². Corners as four vec2 pad uniforms (TL, TR, BR, BL; defaults at the frame corners) or a custom panel with draggable handles; add Edge feather and Brightness for blending projectors, and a Grid toggle that draws a test grid to line it up on the wall. Several surfaces: one quad per surface, each with its own corners and a source sub-rect. Tell the person to use Perform for full screen on the projector.

moves.name: GPU instancing
moves.summary: Draw thousands to a million copies of a shape in one call, each with its own position, rotation, scale and color.
moves.summary_ko: 도형 수천~수백만 개를 한 번의 드로우 콜로, 각자 위치·회전·크기·색을 다르게 그려요.
moves.guide: Replace per-object draw loops with one instanced draw. Per-instance data either as attributes (bind the createMesh vao, add a buffer with offset/scale/rotation/color at locations 3+ — 0–2 are a_position, a_normal, a_uv — and gl.vertexAttribDivisor(loc, 1)) or, when a GPU simulation drives them, computed in the vertex shader from gl_InstanceID with texelFetch from a float data texture (ivec2(id % side, id / side)). Draw with mesh.draw(gl.TRIANGLES, count). Rotate by a quaternion or orient along velocity; vary color and phase per instance from a hash of the id; animate in the shader so the CPU uploads nothing per frame. With three.js: InstancedMesh, setMatrixAt/setColorAt, instanceMatrix.needsUpdate. Keep 2D scenes 2D (orthographic, instanced quads). Uniforms: Count (select up to 100k–1M), Spread, Scale, Jitter. Publish the count with ctx.publish.

moves.name: Shadow mapping
moves.summary: Real cast shadows from a light: shapes shade each other and the ground.
moves.summary_ko: 광원에서 실제 그림자를 드리워 형태끼리, 바닥에 그림자가 생겨요.
moves.guide: Depth pass from the light: a directional light uses an orthographic projection fitted to the scene bounds (mat4 ortho or perspective with a tight frustum), rendered into a DEPTH_COMPONENT24 depth texture you create yourself (texImage2D + framebufferTexture2D; createPingPong's depth is a renderbuffer you can't sample), 2048², with gl.cullFace(FRONT) or slope-scaled bias against acne. Main pass: transform the world position by lightViewProj, sample with a sampler2DShadow (TEXTURE_COMPARE_MODE = COMPARE_REF_TO_TEXTURE, LINEAR filter gives 2×2 PCF for free) and a 16-tap Poisson disk for soft edges; widen the radius with distance to the occluder for a PCSS feel. Add a ground plane so shadows read, and a little ambient so shadowed sides aren't black. Uniforms: Light direction (pad), Softness, Bias.

moves.name: Screen-space reflections
moves.summary: Reflections of what's on screen in glossy floors and surfaces.
moves.summary_ko: 화면에 보이는 것을 광택 있는 바닥과 표면에 반사해요.
moves.guide: Needs a G-buffer: color (HDR) plus view-space normal and depth (createPingPong count 2, RGBA16F). Add a glossy floor if there is none, so the effect shows. SSR pass: from each reflective pixel march along reflect(viewDir, normal) in view space, projecting to screen each step (32–64 steps with growing stride, then 6–8 binary-search refinements on a hit where ray depth passes the buffer depth within a thickness); sample color at the hit. Fade by screen-edge distance, by how much the ray faces the camera, by distance travelled and by roughness (mip-blur the color buffer for rough surfaces); fall back to a sky/env color where it misses. Composite with Fresnel weighting. Uniforms: Reflectivity, Roughness, Steps.

moves.name: God rays
moves.summary: Shafts of light streaming past the shapes toward the camera.
moves.summary_ko: 형태 사이로 빛줄기가 카메라 쪽으로 쏟아져 나와요.
moves.guide: Render an occlusion buffer at half resolution: the light source as a bright disc (its screen position from projecting the 3D light with the view-projection, or a pad uniform for 2D) and every scene object in black. Radial-blur it toward the light (GPU Gems 3 ch. 13: 64–100 samples along the vector to the light, density ~0.9, weight ~0.6, decay ~0.96, exposure), then add it over the scene with additive blending, tinted by the light color. Fade out when the light leaves the screen or goes behind the camera. Uniforms: Intensity, Decay, Light position (pad), Color.

moves.name: Motion blur
moves.summary: Streak fast motion like a camera shutter, for smoother, more filmic movement.
moves.summary_ko: 빠른 움직임을 카메라 셔터처럼 번지게 해 더 영화적으로 만들어요.
moves.guide: Pick by scene: (a) 3D: write per-pixel screen velocity (current minus previous clip position, keep last frame's view-projection and model matrices) into a target, then 8–16 taps along it in a post pass, clamped to a max length from the frame height; (b) particles/2D: temporal accumulation in an RGBA16F ping-pong, out = mix(current, prev, Shutter) — cheap and smooth; (c) offline recordings: render several sub-frames per frame by stepping time in small increments and averaging (only when the scene can be evaluated at arbitrary time). Uniforms: Shutter, Samples.

moves.name: Color grading (LUT)
moves.summary: Film looks: lift/gamma/gain, temperature, a 3D LUT from a .cube file.
moves.summary_ko: 리프트·감마·게인, 색온도, .cube LUT로 영화 같은 톤을 입혀요.
moves.guide: Render the scene into a target, then a grading pass in linear light: white balance (temperature/tint), lift/gamma/gain (three color wheels as color uniforms), saturation and contrast around 0.18 grey, then ACES and sRGB. Looks as a select (Neutral, Teal & orange, Bleach bypass, Warm film, Cold night). If the person uploads a .cube LUT, parse it in setup (asset_read or fetch text; skip comments, read LUT_3D_SIZE and the triplets) into a 3D texture (texImage3D RGB16F, LINEAR) and sample it after tonemapping; blend by Amount. Uniforms: Look (select), Amount, Temperature, Saturation, Contrast.

moves.name: CRT / VHS
moves.summary: Old screens and tapes: curvature, scanlines, chroma bleed, tracking noise.
moves.summary_ko: 옛날 모니터와 비디오테이프 느낌: 곡률, 스캔라인, 색 번짐, 트래킹 노이즈.
moves.guide: Post pass over the rendered scene. CRT: barrel distortion of the uv (k ≈ 0.1), scanlines from the frame height (sin(uv.y·h·π/2) at ~h/2 lines), an RGB aperture-grille or shadow mask at the pixel scale, phosphor glow (blurred copy added), vignette and slight flicker. VHS: chroma bleed (convert to YIQ, low-pass I/Q horizontally with ~6 taps, back to RGB), per-line horizontal jitter from hash(line, time), tracking bands of noise drifting vertically, head-switching wobble in the bottom 3%, a little tape noise. Style select switches CRT / VHS / both. Uniforms: Style, Curvature, Scanlines, Noise.

moves.name: Slit-scan
moves.summary: Show different moments in different parts of the frame, so motion smears through time.
moves.summary_ko: 화면의 부분마다 서로 다른 시점을 보여 줘서 움직임이 시간 속으로 늘어져요.
moves.guide: Keep a ring buffer of the last N frames in a TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY (RGBA8, N 64–128, layers at a reduced size such as 512 on the long side; render the current frame into layer frame % N with framebufferTextureLayer). Display pass: per pixel pick a delay d = Depth × map(x, y) — horizontal, vertical, radial from the center or a slow noise field (select) — and sample layer (frame − d) mod N, interpolating between two layers for smoothness. Reallocate on ctx.resized. Memory is N × w × h × 4 bytes; publish it. Uniforms: Delay depth (frames), Direction (select), Smooth.

moves.name: Kaleidoscope
moves.summary: Fold the picture into mirrored wedges around a center, turning slowly.
moves.summary_ko: 중심을 기준으로 화면을 거울 조각으로 접어 천천히 돌아가게 해요.
moves.guide: Post pass over the rendered scene: convert to polar coordinates around Center (aspect-corrected), fold the angle into a wedge of 2π/N with alternate wedges mirrored (a = abs(mod(a, 2w) − w)), rotate over time, optionally zoom recursively (sample at r·Zoom with fract for an infinite tunnel). Variants by select: radial N-fold, 4-way mirror, hexagonal tiling. Uniforms: Segments, Rotation speed, Zoom, Center (pad), Mode.

moves.name: Domain warping
moves.summary: Warp space with layered noise for marbled, liquid, organic distortion.
moves.summary_ko: 겹친 노이즈로 공간을 비틀어 마블링 같은 유기적인 왜곡을 만들어요.
moves.guide: Warp the lookup coordinates of the existing field or image with layered fbm (Inigo Quilez: q = fbm(p), r = fbm(p + 4q + t·0.1), sample the original at p + Amount·r; use ctx.utils.glsl.FBM / SIMPLEX_3D). For a rendered scene, render it into a target first and displace its uv. Color can also take |q| and |r| for marbling. Animate slowly; keep Amount modest so the piece stays recognisable. Uniforms: Amount, Scale, Speed, Octaves.

moves.name: Boids / flocking
moves.summary: A flock of agents with separation, alignment and cohesion, drawn to the scene's shapes.
moves.summary_ko: 분리·정렬·응집 규칙으로 움직이는 무리가 장면의 형태 쪽으로 몰려들어요.
moves.guide: Positions and velocities in RGBA32F ping-pong textures (up to ~16k agents in WebGL2; WebGPU compute for more). Neighbors: brute force over a texel neighborhood is too slow past ~4k, so bin agents into a coarse grid texture (scatter with gl.POINTS into a count/average target) and read the averages per cell for alignment and cohesion; separation from the 3×3 cells around. Add attraction toward the scene's bright regions (sample a low-res render of it) and toward/away from the mouse, limit speed and turn rate. Draw instanced triangles oriented along velocity (gl_InstanceID → texelFetch), colored by speed or by the scene underneath. Uniforms: Count, Separation, Alignment, Cohesion, Speed, Attraction.

moves.name: Fluid simulation
moves.summary: Stable-fluids smoke and ink that the scene stirs and the mouse can push.
moves.summary_ko: 장면과 마우스가 휘젓는 스테이블 플루이드 연기·잉크를 만들어요.
moves.guide: Use the structure of the oss-webgl-fluid example (catalog_get webgl-fluid-simulation for its scene): velocity RG16F at ~128 on the short side and dye RGBA16F at ~1024, curl → vorticity confinement → divergence → 20 Jacobi pressure iterations → gradient subtract → advect velocity and dye. Inject from the current scene: render it into a target, add it into the dye scaled by Inject each frame (or splat where it's bright or moving), and push velocity along its luminance gradient; mouse drags add splats. Display dye with the scene's palette; add bloom lightly. Uniforms: Viscosity (velocity dissipation), Dye fade, Curl, Inject, Splat force.

moves.name: Cloth simulation
moves.summary: Hang the picture on a cloth that waves in the wind and can be grabbed.
moves.summary_ko: 화면을 천에 걸어 바람에 흔들리고 마우스로 잡아당길 수 있게 해요.
moves.guide: A 48–96² particle grid simulated with Verlet (ctx.utils.createVerletSystem, or your own: structural, shear and bend constraints, 4–8 relaxation iterations, fixed dt 1/60), top edge pinned, gravity, wind from noise over time, the mouse grabs the nearest particle (project its ray with the orbit camera). Recompute normals per frame, upload positions/normals into the mesh buffers (bufferSubData), and texture the cloth with the scene rendered into a target, two-sided lighting (flip the normal on back faces). Optional tearing when a constraint stretches past a limit. Uniforms: Wind, Stiffness, Gravity.

moves.name: Metaballs / marching cubes
moves.summary: Blobby isosurfaces that merge and split, extracted from the scene's points or fields.
moves.summary_ko: 장면의 점이나 필드에서 서로 붙었다 떨어지는 말랑한 등위면을 뽑아내요.
moves.guide: Build a scalar field from the scene: each particle or bright point contributes r²/d² (metaballs), or use the existing density. Two routes: raymarch the field directly in a fullscreen pass (sphere-trace with a conservative step, cheap for < 64 balls passed as a uniform array or a data texture), or extract a mesh each frame on the CPU with marching cubes on a 48–96³ grid (the isosurface catalog entry, as in the oss-isosurface example) and draw it with smooth normals from the field gradient. Shade with the PBR or toon moves for a finished look. Uniforms: Threshold, Resolution, Blob size.

moves.name: Voronoi mosaic
moves.summary: Rebuild the picture from Voronoi cells, denser where there's detail.
moves.summary_ko: 디테일이 많은 곳일수록 촘촘한 보로노이 셀로 화면을 다시 짜요.
moves.guide: Render the scene into a target. Seeds: read a low-res copy back (readPixels at ~160 px, a few times a second) to place seeds with density proportional to edge magnitude (rejection sampling), or use an in-shader jittered grid for a uniform mosaic. Fill each cell with the color at its seed (or the cell average via a second pass), darken borders by (d2 − d1) to the second-nearest seed, and drift seeds slowly with noise. For an exact CPU version with polygons, d3-delaunay (catalog). Use jump flooding (log2 passes) for thousands of seeds on the GPU. Uniforms: Cells, Border, Jitter, Detail bias.

moves.name: Glass & refraction
moves.summary: Turn the shapes into glass: refraction, dispersion, Fresnel reflections.
moves.summary_ko: 형태를 유리로 바꿔 굴절, 분산, 프레넬 반사를 줘요.
moves.guide: Raster: render the background (everything but the glass) into a target; draw the glass objects sampling it at screen uv + refract(viewDir, normal, 1/IOR).xy × Thickness (estimate thickness from a back-face depth pass), Fresnel (Schlick, F0 0.04) mix with a sharp environment reflection, three samples at slightly different IORs for chromatic dispersion, a light tint and blur for frosted glass (mip of the background). SDF scenes: on hit, refract into the volume and march the negated SDF to the exit point, refract out, then shade the background along the exit ray; repeat for 2 bounces max. Uniforms: IOR, Dispersion, Tint, Frost.

moves.name: GPU particles (WebGPU compute)
moves.summary: Move the simulation to compute shaders: a million particles at full frame rate.
moves.summary_ko: 시뮬레이션을 컴퓨트 셰이더로 옮겨 파티클 백만 개를 실시간으로 돌려요.
moves.guide: This rewrites the scene for backend "webgpu" (see the WebGPU section of the scene reference): particle state in a storage buffer (vec4 position + vec4 velocity, 1M entries), a compute pass with @workgroup_size(64) integrating forces (curl noise, attraction to the scene's shapes from a texture of the old render, mouse), and a render pass drawing instanced quads that read the storage buffer by instance_index, additive blending into an rgba16float target, then a fullscreen tonemap to the canvas. Keep the old look's colors and controls. If WebGPU isn't available, WebGL2 transform feedback is the fallback. Uniforms: Count (select), Speed, Size.

moves.name: Tilt-shift
moves.summary: Blur above and below a sharp band so the scene looks like a tiny model.
moves.summary_ko: 선명한 띠 위아래를 흐려 장면이 작은 모형처럼 보이게 해요.
moves.guide: Post pass over the rendered scene: blur radius grows with vertical distance from a focus band (Focus y, Band width), applied as a two-pass separable Gaussian whose sigma varies per pixel, or a golden-angle bokeh blur with ~32 taps for nicer highlights; boost saturation and contrast a little for the miniature look. Works best looking down at a 3D scene from above, so suggest raising the camera. Uniforms: Focus, Band width, Blur, Saturation.
